classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the same shape's area can be expressed using two different base–height pairs, match each perpendicular height to its base, and equate the expressions to find the unknown length.

spec.description: Unshaded parallelogram leaning right. Horizontal base 17.2 cm, right sloping side 10 cm, vertical perpendicular height 8 cm, and oblique perpendicular distance a cm from the upper-left vertex to the right side. Retains dimension arrows and both right-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: The same parallelogram has area 17.2 × 8 = 10a. Diagram coordinates are schematic; perpendicular feet and angle marks are derived from the drawn edges.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible; the numerical answer is absent.

answer.worked:
Using the horizontal base:
$$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\A&=17.2\times8\\A&=137.6\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
Using the sloping side as the base:
$$\begin{align*}137.6&=10a\\\frac{137.6}{10}&=a\\13.76\text{ cm}&=a\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded triangle pointing right. Left side 15 mm, lower side 24 mm, and internal perpendicular height 12 mm. The left-side line extends beyond the upper-left vertex to the foot of the external perpendicular distance x mm from the right vertex. Retains all dimension arrows and both right-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: The same triangle has area (24 × 12)/2 = (15x)/2. The x dimension is perpendicular to the extended 15 mm side, distinct from the upper triangle edge. Both perpendicular feet are derived by projection.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible; the numerical answer is absent.

answer.worked:
Using the lower side as the base:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A&=\frac{24\times12}{2}\\A&=144\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$
Using the left side as the base:
$$\begin{align*}144&=\frac{15x}{2}\\288&=15x\\\frac{288}{15}&=x\\19.2\text{ mm}&=x\end{align*}$$
